problem_statement:
**Problem 1.** Fix an integer $n \geq 2$. For which real numbers $x$ is
$$\left\lfloor nx \right\rfloor - \sum_{k=1}^{n} \frac{\lfloor kx \rfloor}{k}$$
maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?
official_answer: Maximum value: $\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3} + \cdots + \frac{1}{n} = H_n - 1$, where $H_n$ is the $n$-th harmonic number. Achieved exactly when the fractional part of $x$ satisfies $\{x\} \geq 1 - \frac{1}{n}$.
official_answer_natural: The maximum value of the expression is the partial harmonic sum starting from k=2: 1/2 + 1/3 + ... + 1/n. This maximum is attained exactly when the fractional part of x is at least 1 - 1/n.
grading_notes: A complete solution must (1) identify the correct maximum value (1/2 + 1/3 + ... + 1/n, equivalently H_n - 1) and (2) characterize the full set of x values achieving it (fractional part of x at least 1 - 1/n). Partial credit if only one direction is proven (upper bound vs construction). Common pitfalls: solving only specific small n; conflating the floor sum with the harmonic series identity; sign errors on the harmonic sum index.
external_reference: Solutions in Evan Chen's USAMO 2026 notes §1.1 (2026-05-16): https://web.evanchen.cc/exams/USAMO-2026-notes.pdf
